Cotenancy/fiduciary dispute over renewal of a manufacturing-property lease among heirs. Concerns cotenant duties and renewal doctrine, not short-term letting or lodging/boarding practice.

cite: Edgar A. Levy Leasing Co. v. Siegel, 230 N.Y. 634
notes: Emergency Rent Laws case sustaining rent-reasonableness defenses for ordinary 2-year apartment leases (companion to People ex rel. Durham Realty Corp. v. La Fetra). The statute expressly EXEMPTS 'a lodging or rooming house occupied under a hiring of a week or less' (Sec. 9) — short-term lodging is carved OUT, not regulated, so the case does not adjudicate the letting/lodging practice itself. Flagged for possible Planner interest re: the McLaughlin dissent's 'vendor of space' framing of letting as an ordinary private business, but not coded as relevant per the passing-mention rule.
Municipal police-power case sustaining a garage oil-separator regulation; no connection to lodging or letting of dwellings.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Facts recite that a prior tenant, Harriet Bohm, privately arranged with the new tenant's wife to retain two rooms of the dwelling 'for which she paid a stipulated consideration' — a lodger-type letting for pay. But the court's actual holding concerns landlord-tenant possession law: the duty to eject a holdover stranger from part of demised premises falls on the tenant, not the landlord. The letting arrangement's legal character is never adjudicated or characterized by the court, so treated as passing background per the relevance rule rather than a doctrinal holding on the letting practice.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Holdover-tenant case on whether a landlord may treat a tenant remaining past a one-year term as a tenant for another year or a trespasser. Ordinary landlord-tenant doctrine, unrelated to lodging/boarding-house practice.

Ejectment for breach of a lease covenant requiring the tenant to obey orders of municipal departments, including the tenement house department. Concerns a landlord's re-entry right for building/sanitary-code non-compliance, not the practice or regulation of short-term room-letting.
False-imprisonment action arising from a peddler's-license dispute over obstructing a public street with a sales stand; no connection to lodging or letting of dwellings.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: Under Laws of 1905, chapter 206, a hotel/apartment-hotel/boarding-or-lodging-house keeper's lien on a guest's property is defeated only by knowledge or notice, at the time the property was brought onto the premises, that it belonged to a third party; notice received afterward does not retroactively defeat the lien for charges already accrued.
